answer: Randomized assignment pools: each epoch, a verifiable random function assigns agents to tasks, and no one knows the mapping until the seed is published. An attacker cannot precompute which identities will cluster near a juniper node's work, so clones must be funded and maintained blind across all pools. The cost is per-identity upkeep—bandwidth, latency bonds, and idle capacity—paid every epoch in an oasis region the attacker cannot predict. Residual risk sits in the river of late-joining identities, so a short commit-delay window forces each new agent to wait one full epoch before assignment.
